_comment: The lottery card graphic. Figma's `Card` (14591:60095) is artwork plus an ID overlaid — three fixed sizes, each with its own raster. The card face is an asset; the component is the asset plus text.

_verified_from.scope: all 3 sizes, artwork nodes and the bound text style
_verified_from.result: L 326x205, M 154x96, S 76x48, radius 0. The face is an IMAGE fill at each size — three different rasters, not one scaled. The ID reads `typography/body/l-med` (16/24 Medium) in `card-fg-white` with a 10 gap, placed absolutely at (22,165) on L and (10,72) on M. S carries no text.

_source.sizes and id offsets: Read off each variant. The ID is positioned absolutely, not laid out, and the two offsets are not the same fraction of the card — 6.7%/80.5% on L against 6.5%/75% on M — so they are held per size rather than derived.
_source.artwork: Exported at 3x per size into ui/assets/logos as `card-lottery-l|m|s`. Three files because Figma uses three different images, not one scaled.

_figma_gaps.id-is-not-laid-out: The ID is absolutely positioned on each size instead of being an auto-layout child, which is why its offsets had to be copied per size rather than expressed once.
_figma_gaps.large-face-is-heavy: `card-lottery-l` is 272KB at 3x. It is a detailed illustration at 326px wide; if it ships on a list screen, a 2x export or a WebP would be worth considering.

_figma_icons._comment: The icons Figma instantiates for this component, read 2026-08-20 by walking the instance tree and keeping every main component whose parent set is `icons`. An icon Figma hides by default belongs in `icons` only when this component implements the state that reveals it; otherwise it is recorded under _figma_gaps instead, so the gate is not asking for a feature nobody built.

nodes.note: This component draws no icon at all in Figma. Recorded so that one appearing later has to be justified rather than slipping in.
